I can't praise this game enough. If you grew up playing console or cabinet games this game is for you. It's what would happen if Blizzard decided to make a 2D 16bit platformer. Nearly every good aspect of the ancient platformers (Super Mario, Zelda, Contra, Castlevania, Ducktales) are represented along with a great period soundtrack.

I played through in roughly 15 hours, (much of it offline so steam didn't report it well.) The storypieces weren't a detraction being in text (with no speech) it was immersive in the nostalgic sense. I can see how a younger player might not get it, but if you ever played the classic platformers you will find this entertaining.
This is one of the best deals. Four amazing games for the price of one. Yacht Club really went above and beyond with this.

Very fun game, a little frustating at times and the main story was a little short. But other than that it was a great renditions of oldschool game like megaman. 

Very fun platformer with great pixel art and soundtrack.

Oh my god... this game... it is one of my favorite games of all time! I played this on the WiiU consule single player, and co-op with my brother using the shovel knight amiibo, and I loved it so much that I just had to buy it for steam to hold on to forever and forever! It is controller compatible, and it runs really well on the pc. The characters in this game are wonderful, the soundtrack is marvelous, and the graphics and stages are so nostalgic of the good old platformer days. This has become my favorite platformer. This game just grabs a hold of you and you can't let go. I never want to let go of this game ever.

10/10
Well, I didn't expect to like this as much as I did. Great music, level design, progression, challenging battles. The different items you can use make it fun too.

I can't reccomend Shovel Knight enough. You've got amazing gameplay, level design, music, and an awesome tribute to old school platforming. The devs have been really great to their customers as well; there's even a new campaign coming out next year!

I've nominated this game for the Labour of Love award for the 2018 Steam Awards.

Buy this game! Just do it! This game is a spectacular call back to the classic Mega Man series, with maybe some classic Castlevania in the mix too. It has a wonderfully simple story, with funny, creative, and likable characters. The experience is even better if you're into fantasy/medieval story settings. All this accompanied by an amazing soundtrack, I dare say it rivals the best of 8bit tracks out there. Truly a modern platforming masterpiece. I can not recommend this enough, you are in for a treat.

A true homage to the retro community with every aspect, from music to the gameplay, handled in the top-notch sense. There are some lessons to be learned from these guys. And what's more, free downloadable contents is the cherry on the pie.

The gameplay is a solid platformer. In terms of narrative, expect the tone and complexity that comes with your main character wielding a shovel and using it to defeat evil. Each campaign (there are four) get progressively better, so if you don't like Shovel of Hope, go to King of Cards. Also, each subsequent campaign is a prequel to the last, so I recommend playing them backwards so you catch all the continuities.

Ever have I felt heroic while holding a shovel before, until I played this game.

The gameplay is really simple and you get more stuff along the way. Music makes you wanna go dig ground outside or just go travel the world. With your shovel. While dressing up as a knight. Also the story is great and filled with lovely characters.

The game didn't let me down at any point. The lenght of the game was perfect. It felt like a Megaman game. But perhaps even better than that.

This my favourite game of all time, absolutely worth it. This game has everything good about old school platformers with the streamlining and level design of the current generation. This $40 game features:

-3 full platforming games
-A full smash-like spinoff
-Amazing music

Shovel Knight is, in one word, fantastic.

Let's be clear: if you've never been a 2D platformer player, this probably won't sway you. The game requires skill, but has a decent learning curve. On the other hand, it seldom holds your hand through the different obstacles and platforming mechanics. But it's a very enjoyable ride, because you're playing a very cute game with fun dialogue and characters. Don't expect much of a storyline in the original campaign, but it's still nice.

As for Plague of Shadows, it's an amazing free DLC. It plays very, very differently from the Shovel Knight campaign, as Plague Knight throws potions and can sometimes do four jumps in a row using different items and mechanics. Plague of Shadows has more of a storyline, and it's cute-as-heck.

Shovel Knight is clearly a labour of love, and I can't recommend it enough.

An amazing game, I recommend it. It may look like I haven't played much, but that is because I played it on another system, so I have really played all the DLC up until now. The platforming is amazing and unique, and the combat is so refreshing. Each DLC has something new to offer and feels like a different game. The story isn't the main focus and it is good enough to keep you invested, which adds on to the experience. Overall, you need to get this game. Can't wait for King Knight DLC.

This game is great. It has some beautiful pixel art and amazing music. The gameplay is very refined and polished. With the great level design it makes a game that hours can be put into. Plus, it's basically 3 games (4 soon) games in one. The different storylines are also really good. If you are into platformers definetly check this game out.

Honestly, this pretty much does a lot right of being a nostalgic retro game that most indie devs seem to try to replicate, but only do it the aesthesis of those games and not gameplay. This feels like it belongs on the NES, or even some Gameboy games.

This is seriously a real good attempt at being those types of games. It is very worth the price and I can whole heart-fully recommend it on Wii U or 3DS, which is if you have either one of them, just for an all round fun experience.

I really dig it.

If you like action platformers this is the game for you. Good visuals, music and gameplay, this game has it all. Free updates even added completely new storylines which are their own games pretty much. Very much recommended!

Entertaining game that pays homage to Mega Man with the varied weapons and challenging levels and bosses. Also, the free DLC that's been provided over the years have made the game more enjoyable as the expansions aren't just reskins but reworked levels for the new games.

Not that this game needs anyone else telling people how good it is, but it's really a blast! If you dig old-school platformers, this is about as good as it gets. The people who are complaining about it's difficulty must have missed the age that inspired this game, because back in the NES days EVERY game was "Souls-like". That's why the original NES controller was built to withstand the apocolypse.

I have got to say this is one of the best platforming games out there. This has all of the crisp feel and retro style graphics that the old games used to have, but without all of the difficulties. You can select the relics, change your movement while jumping, and more without all of the stuff that would normally discourage someone from playing a platforming game. Yes, it requires skill. Does it require hours and hours of gameplay, like many triple A games to be good at? No I just beat the game at the time of the review, and I had a blast. This is an amazing game and I highly recommend playing it. I also wouldn't watch a ton of guides on how to do the boss fights, as it is fairly simple to figure out for yourself, and it is more fun to actually play the game trial and error style, rather than copying what someone else has already done. I come from a background of FPS games, and only having played one other platforming game (which felt sluggish and hard to learn. It punished you for every slight mistake, to the point where the game was no longer fun anymore) and Shovel Knight has convinced me to continue playing platforming games. This is absolutely without a doubt one of, if not the best platforming title on the Steam store.
Really fun worth every penny. Don't buy any DLC other than this "Treasure Trove" thing as I'm sure there's something else you can buy. This has it all.
Every character in this game, especially the playable ones, thinks they're better than everyone else, and in each campaign you prove them all wrong but as a different person.

I have to say I am really loving this game. Love the stories, the challenging platforming, and all the abilities and things you can do in this game. However the one thing I don't like is when you die you leave three floating coin bags, which contain gold you collected. This is fine, however the coin bags spread out to different spots, which may be hard to get to without getting killed again or my personal favorite they appear off the screen. Their's difficult and then theirs being cheap, which is what this is doing. I am still going to give this product a thumbs up, because it has only that one negative.

Fun and overall cute retro-styled platformer about a knight with a very obvious gimmick of having a shovel instead of a sword. And they do hang a lampshade on it. I don't have to DIG deep to find good things to say about this game. Tons of content, new campaigns with unique playable characters being added as time goes along, the shovel allows for interesting mechanics to be implemented, the game allows you to genderswap everyone for your pleasure, and the visual aesthetic faithfully recreates NES graphics without being forced into the same limits as the NES. This means tons of visuals and only a few extra colors over the NES. Runs at 60 fps, feels tight and smooth, controls are easy to configure, no problems from the technical side.
Played this with a SNES controller adapter and it felt like I'd traveled to some sort of alternate dimension where everything was quasi-1980s in the 2010s. Really good game. You'd only really dislike this game if you're not a fan of NES-era graphics.

One of the greatest games ever made. This comes with four separate campaigns, an iffy platform fighter, challenges, and now a mix and match gender feature. There are so many way to play, and so many things to enjoy. It controls are amazing, but I was shocked how good everything else was. Outstanding music, beautiful pixel art, and a fantastic story. Four stories part of the same timeline with many twists and turns. With great portrayals of grief, greed, and unrequited love. Great writing and worldbuilding was the last thing I expected out of Shovel Knight. It's a gift that keeps on giving. A must-play if you haven't already.
the game was fantastic when it only had shovel knight, and now there's 4x the content with each new story campaign being better than the last

Shovel Knight captures the essence of retro 2D platformers of yesteryear and presents it to a modern audience with polished art, a stylish, unforgettable soundtrack, and tough-as-nails gameplay that will delight anyone fond of the hard NES game era. An absolute classic in the history of games.

I recommend this game with the following warnings:

1. it is very hard and can feel like bullshit at times. If you lose a lot, just reset the level. It's an option and not your fault.

2. the default controls are bad for controller. (I suggest unbinding Shovel-Down from analog, and tying it to RB. I also recommend unbinding Relic usage from Up+X and making it LB. This makes the game MUCH easier to control when you character doesn't do something unintended.)

3. don't sleep on relics, they make some boss fights very manageable (phase locket is OP)

Imagine if someone put Duck Tales, Classic Megaman, Classic Castlevania, and Super Mario Bros. 3 into a blender, and you'll get something like Shovel Knight....or a video game smoothie, whatever works. This game is fun and challenging. A fantastic platformer. If you are a fan of platformers and classic games from the NES and SNES era, this game would make a fantabulous addition to your library.

I've finished Shovel of Hope so far, and I had a really good time for the most part. While I do think insta-kill pits and spikes are a bit unfair (especially on the airship), I liked the platforming. This was my first impression of any game like this, and so Im glad I enjoyed it. The game does get pretty hard after a bit, and sometimes frustrating, but nothing impossible. The boss rush at the end isn't that hard, I beat it first try. The controls weren't too bad, thought they were annoying given certain conditions (like the airship). Something to note is that the game was abnormally fast when Vsync was on for me. I first played on my Steam deck, before moving to my Macbook Neo. The problem was fixed by turning Vsync off though. Overall, I enjoyed the first game a lot, and would recommend you try it out.
By the way, just use the propeller dagger, it's the best.

If you liked challenging NES platformers such as Castlevania, Megaman, and Zelda 2, you'll enjoy Shovel Knight. It's quite challenging, but there are plenty of checkpoints throughout the levels, and you get infinite lives, so as to keep frustration levels low.

The levels are designed intelligently, in that new game mechanics are gradually introduced - you might learn how to deal with bouncy squid on one screen, and then on the next screen you'll have to bounce on the squid to get over some spikes.

The music is excellent in chiptune style, reminiscent of the NES games I mentioned earlier. There also seem to be references to Megaman and other games - for instance there is a boss who resembles Enker from the Megaman series in terms of his attacks.

Overall, this is a well made game which is quite challenging, but not too frustratingly impossible.

You know, after the megaman franchise was over, I didnt think I could find another game to replace it.... I was wrong. Shovel man is a great game in all aspects. For starters it runs on low end PCs, Its fun, its actually decently hard, and all in all theres a pretty decent story line, and heres the kicker, ITS ONLY $15.

The gameplay makes me salty because I'm bad at platformers, but I'm more patient with this game than most because of how charming the world is. From being given a preachy lecture on how you should be careful what you buy to an npc who's only job is to tell you puns.

My only complaint is that I wish exiting the game wouldn't lose you your in level checkpoints. If it didn't, and I was able to pick up the game again without missing a beat, the required playsession time could be much shorter, which is good for me because I like to play games in short bursts.

If you ever get bored DIGGING through your game library and want something truly GROUNDBREAKING, than you'll find that shovel knight is a GEM of a game.

It also has got the concept of good boss fights IN SPADES.
Love this game. Been playing it since close to release and love all of it. Would highly recommend if you are a fan of platformers.

Everything it's hyped up to be and more. I have a quibble in that the two expansion games aren't quite as tight as the core experience....but that's a pretty TINY quibble considering I got both of those games for free with the core experience. Even for what they are, they're still well above the average game that appears to coast on retro-appeal.

A solid experience, top to bottom, and well worth the price.

Shovel Knight is my favorite game released during the past few years. It does everything a 2D platformer should do right: great graphics, great music, challenging level design, and worthwhile boss encounters. This game combines all the best elements of the classics of the 2D platforming genre (e.g., Mega Man, Castlevania, Ducktales) with modern conveniences (i.e., level checkpoints). Also, you actually get multiple games in one as you can play the alternate storyline of Plague Knight! Get shoveling, dear readers, and play this fantastic game!

So, educated peoples who used to make games back in the day were trying to find ways to get good money and they were all like: "What if we made a 2d platform game like Mega Man but it's about knights with odd weapons?"

Shovel Knight is a game where you are a knight with a shovel looking to save his girlfriend so he can have a purpose in life again. Also it's supposed to be remniscent of a NES [Nintendo Entertainment System, if you don't know] game. It has semi-8bit graphics, chiptune music, and takes elements from many masterful NES games. Thus, if you are okay with NES platformers, then you will be okay if not super satisfied with this game. Also. THAT SOUNDTRACK. It's truly a wonder to behold. Also, if you like local multiplayer, the Wii U version has it already and the PC version will be getting it soon, so feel free to buy this if sometime in the future you feel like LAN partying it up with your friends. Do yourself a favor and buy this if you have not already and if you already have it, dude, why are you looking at reviews for a game you own when you could be playing it or doing literally anything else?

TL;DR IT'S A LONG LOST GAME FROM THE NES NEVER RELEASED UNTIL NOW AND IF YOU LIKED THEM NES GAMES GO BUY THIS YOU'LL ENJOY IT

Shovel Knight is one of those games that you CONSTANTLY come back to for replayablity value. The game is widely approved (as it has also branched off into physical ports) and it's because it reminds everyone of those very hard yet memorable games from their childhood. It's story is easy to grasp, and it has just enough difficulty to make it that much more enjoyable. The music is catchy, the characters have their own quirks and it makes the whole thing that much better.
Gameplay is fun and simple. Additionally, the story is pretty cute. Also, the second DLC is quite awesome

Complaints are few, mostly about the controls and the platforming.
